## Which file do I download?

| Your device | Download this file |
|---|---|
| 📱 **Android phone or tablet** | **`ExpenseTracker-Android.apk`** |
| 💻 **Mac with Apple chip** (M1, M2, M3, M4 — most Macs from 2021 on) | **`ExpenseTracker-Mac-AppleSilicon.dmg`** |
| 💻 **Older Mac with Intel chip** | **`ExpenseTracker-Mac-Intel.dmg`** |
| 🖥 **Windows 10 / 11** | **`ExpenseTracker-Windows-Setup.exe`** |
| 🐧 **Linux** | **`ExpenseTracker-Linux.AppImage`** |
| 🍎 **iPhone / iPad** | No download — open the [web app](https://thrishankkuntimaddi.github.io/ExpenseTracker/) in Safari → Share → **Add to Home Screen** |

Not sure which Mac you have? → Apple menu → **About This Mac**. "Chip: Apple M…" means Apple chip; "Processor: Intel" means Intel.

*"Source code" zips, the `.app.tar.gz` files and `latest.json` are for GitHub and the apps' automatic updates — you don't need them.*

**Updates are automatic.** Once installed, the apps keep themselves up to date: Android receives most updates over the air (no reinstall), the desktop apps download updates in the background and ask to restart, and the website updates on its own.

All versions use the same account and stay in sync. Sign in with Google or with your email and password.

## How to install

**Android**
1. Download `ExpenseTracker-Android.apk` on your phone and tap it.
2. If asked, allow your browser to *install unknown apps*. Chrome may say the file "can harm your device" — it says this for every app that doesn't come from the Play Store.
3. Updates: install the newer APK over the old one; your data stays (it's in your account).

**Mac**
1. Open the `.dmg` and drag **ExpenseTracker** into **Applications**.
2. Open it. macOS will say it "can't be verified" because the app isn't registered with Apple (that costs $99/year).
3. Go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down, and click **Open Anyway** next to ExpenseTracker. You only do this once.

**Windows**
1. Run `ExpenseTracker-Windows-Setup.exe`.
2. If "Windows protected your PC" appears, click **More info → Run anyway** (shown for apps without a paid code-signing certificate). You only do this once.

**Linux**
1. `chmod +x ExpenseTracker-Linux.AppImage` and run it.

On desktop the app stays in the menu bar / system tray after you close its window — click the icon to bring it back.
